handbookNote: Ohio Real Estate Broker license exam. Exam vendor: WebSearch was exhausted for this session before a primary-source PSI/Pearson VUE candidate-handbook PDF could be independently fetched (com.ohio.gov's own candidate-information-bulletin page returned HTTP 404 on roughly a dozen distinct WebFetch attempts across multiple URL patterns -- the Ohio Department of Commerce site appears to block automated fetches -- and web.archive.org is not reachable from this environment either). PSI Services is reasonably well-corroborated as Ohio's exam vendor from two independent secondary sources fetched directly (usrealtytraining.com's Ohio exam guide, which names 'PSI Exams Online' as the testing provider and gives Ohio SALESPERSON exam figures of 120 questions/80 national+40 state/180 minutes/70% passing each portion, matching a national:state ratio and per-portion-passing structure independently confirmed via a dedicated research subagent's WebFetch of OAC rule 1301:5-1-05, which establishes Ohio's exam as split into a national portion (two-thirds of the exam) and an Ohio-state-specific portion (one-third), each requiring 75% to pass for the BROKER exam and 70% for the salesperson exam, within an eligibility window before results/portions expire; and estatepass.ai's Ohio guide, which gives Ohio BROKER exam figures of 115 questions/180 minutes/75% passing, consistent with the OAC-confirmed 75% broker passing threshold) -- but this is corroborated-secondary-source triangulation, NOT an independently fetched primary PSI/Pearson VUE PDF, and the exact national-vs-state SPLIT of the broker exam's 115 questions (as opposed to the salesperson exam's confirmed 80/40 split) was not pinned down to an exact integer pair this pass; treat exam_question_count/exam_duration_sec/pass_percent in the companion oh_re_broker_registry.sql as corroborated-but-not-primary-confirmed, flagged accordingly rather than presented as fully verified. Ohio licensure prerequisites were CONFIRMED directly via WebFetch of codes.ohio.gov (Ohio's official state code publisher): ORC 4735.07 requires a broker applicant to be at least 18 years old (the same minimum as Ohio's salesperson license -- Ohio does NOT raise the age minimum for brokers the way some other states do), to have held an Ohio real estate broker's or salesperson's license for at least 2 of the preceding 5 years, and to have either completed at least 20 real estate sales transactions in that period or equivalent experience under Commission rule. Pre-license education for broker applicants licensed on/after August 1, 2001 (independently re-verified via direct WebFetch of ORC 4735.07(B)(6)(b), which resolved an initial hedge over the 'same hours as above' language) totals 240 hours: 40 hours real estate practice, 40 hours Ohio real estate law and civil rights law, 20 hours real estate appraisal, 20 hours real estate finance, plus 30 hours each in financial management, human resource/personnel management, applied business economics, and business law. New brokers must also complete 10 hours of post-licensing instruction within 12 months of license issuance. JUDGMENT CALL, resolved per the build brief's specific instruction to check this: Ohio does NOT have a separate 'principal broker' license tier or a separate principal-broker examination. ORC 4735.081 ('Designation of principal broker') requires every brokerage to designate at least one of its already-licensed brokers to serve as principal broker -- a ROLE/DESIGNATION carrying statutory oversight duties (overseeing brokerage operations; office/branch compliance; displaying the fair-housing statement; handling license renewals and recordkeeping; managing trust/special accounts; developing written agency-relationship policies; ensuring salespersons are paid what they're owed; overseeing advertising compliance; supervising affiliated licensees), not a different license class or a harder/additional exam; a principal broker qualifies through the identical ORC 4735.07-4735.08 broker exam and licensure path as any other broker. A principal broker may delegate day-to-day supervisory duties to a 'management level licensee' under OAC rule 1301:5-6-01, but that delegation does NOT relieve the principal broker of ultimate statutory responsibility for the brokerage's operations -- this distinction, directly analogous to how the pa_re_broker and ny_re_broker banks handled their own states' associate-broker concepts, is concentrated heavily in this bank's bucket 3 (Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees). Per the brief's requirement that broker content go substantially deeper than a generic salesperson bank into broker-specific territory, this 306-question bank concentrates 102 of its 306 questions (33.3%, almost exactly a third) into six broker-specific buckets: Broker Licensure Requirements & Application, Broker Office Management/Branch Offices/Recordkeeping, Broker Supervision/Principal Brokers/Management-Level Licensees, Escrow & Trust Fund Management, Commission/Compensation & Broker-Salesperson Relationships, and License Law/Commission Discipline/Recovery Fund. Real Ohio statute/rule citations, independently verified via direct WebFetch of codes.ohio.gov (Ohio's official Legislative Service Commission-published code site) across this build's research pass and each of six parallel content-authoring passes, include: ORC Chapter 4735 (Real Estate Brokers, Salespersons) Sections 4735.06-4735.081 (broker application, exam qualifications, license-issuance conditions, principal-broker designation), 4735.091 (broker/salesperson may associate with a brokerage as employee OR independent contractor -- Ohio statute explicitly allows either), 4735.13 (definite place of business, license display, branch-office separate licensing and supervision, 3-business-day departure notice, 30-day relocation notice), 4735.16 (advertising: name/brokerage disclosure, 'agent owned' disclosure, no advertising a listed property as 'for sale by owner,' up to $2,500/citation fine), 4735.18(A)'s approximately 40 enumerated grounds for license discipline (misrepresentation, undisclosed dual roles, unearned-commission demands, commingling, the two-different-trust-account-types rule at (A)(26)-(27), 3-year record retention at (A)(24), prompt salesperson-commission payment at (A)(31), 'right-to-list' agreement prohibition at (A)(39), residential wholesaler noncompliance at (A)(40), and more), 4735.24 (earnest-money trust-account handling, 2-year dispute clause with a September 1 return deadline, unclaimed-property reporting to the Ohio director of commerce), 4735.51/4735.55/4735.71 (agency definitions, written representation-agreement requirements including a definite expiration date and negotiable-compensation/blockbusting/HUD-logo disclosures, dual-agency written-consent and confidentiality-walling requirements), 4735.051/4735.052 (complaint investigation and mediation; unlicensed-practice civil penalty up to $1,000/violation), 4735.12 (Real Estate Recovery Fund: renewal-fee-and-interest funding, up to $10/year special assessment if the fund drops below $250,000 on July 1, a $40,000-per-licensee liability cap pro-rated among multiple claimants, and automatic license suspension on any fund payout until full repayment plus statutory interest); OAC rules 1301:5-5-08/-09/-11/-23 (trust-account handling, required records, and the separate property-management trust-account rules, including that a broker's own funds may enter a trust account ONLY to maintain a required minimum balance or cover bank service charges); OAC rules 1301:5-6-01 through -09 (management-level licensees, open houses/referrals, mandatory company policy, agency/fair-housing/blockbusting disclosures, the Consumer Guide to agency relationships, refusal-to-sign handling, the agency disclosure statement, appointment of licensees, and negotiations with a represented party); ORC Chapter 4112, especially 4112.02(H) (Ohio's fair-housing protected classes: race, color, religion, sex, MILITARY STATUS, familial status, ancestry, disability, and national origin -- 9 classes, meaning Ohio ADDS military status and ancestry on top of the federal Fair Housing Act's 7 classes, a strong Ohio-specific differentiator tested explicitly in bucket 8), 4112.021 (credit discrimination) and 4112.024 (narrow religious-organization/fraternal-lodge exemptions); ORC 1335.04 (Ohio's real-property statute of frauds); ORC 2323.07 and the surrounding judicial-sale statutes (CONFIRMING Ohio is a JUDICIAL FORECLOSURE state -- court-ordered sheriff's sale, not a non-judicial trustee-sale process -- and that Ohio real property is conveyed by MORTGAGE, not a deed of trust); ORC Chapter 4763 (Ohio's real estate APPRAISER licensure framework, independently confirmed via WebFetch to be a SEPARATE license from the broker license under Chapter 4735, with its own four-tier structure, Real Estate Appraiser Board, continuing-education, and recovery-fund provisions); ORC Chapter 5321 (Landlord-Tenant Act), especially 5321.16 (security deposits exceeding the greater of $50 or one month's rent accrue 5%/year simple interest if the tenancy runs 6+ months, paid annually, with a 30-day itemized-deduction return deadline and a wrongful-withholding remedy of the withheld amount plus an equal amount in damages plus attorney fees) and 5321.04/5321.05/5321.07/5321.15/5321.17 (landlord/tenant duties, cure-notice procedure, self-help-eviction ban, and 7-day/30-day termination-notice tiers, independently fetched); ORC Chapters 713 (municipal zoning) and 519 (township zoning), independently confirmed to establish Ohio's real structural split between municipal and township zoning authority (including township zoning's voter-approval and 5-member-commission requirements and its agricultural-lot carve-out); ORC 5302.30 (Ohio's residential property disclosure form: 1-4-unit transfers, actual-knowledge-only seller liability standard, and specific exemptions including court-ordered transfers, spousal/family transfers, new/never-occupied construction, and sales to a buyer who already occupied the property 1+ year); and Ohio's two-layer real-property transfer taxation, both independently confirmed via direct statute fetch: the MANDATORY statewide conveyance fee under ORC 319.54(G)(3) ($1.00 per $1,000 of value, or $1 flat, whichever is greater) plus the PERMISSIVE additional county real-property transfer tax under ORC 322.02 (up to $0.30 per $100 / $3.00 per $1,000 by county-commissioner resolution), combining to a possible maximum of $0.40 per $100 / $4.00 per $1,000 in counties levying the full permissive rate -- used for several concrete worked numeric word-problems in the Real Estate Investment & Math bucket. Ohio's real-property-tax homestead-exemption dollar/income figures were explicitly left unconfirmed (flagged as a hedge) rather than guessed, since ORC 323.151 confirmed only the age/disability eligibility definitions and the actual current dollar thresholds live in cross-referenced sections not independently fetched this pass. Ohio's real-estate CLOSING/SETTLEMENT customs are flagged throughout bucket 17 as a HEDGE, not a codified-statute-confirmed fact: multiple WebFetch attempts at the Ohio State Bar Association, the Ohio Land Title Association (whose own domain redirected to an unrelated New York title company site), ALTA's state-affiliate directory, and other title-industry sources all failed to return usable primary or clearly-citable content within this session's tool constraints, so this bank presents Ohio's closing practice (title-agency/escrow-driven, attorney involvement common but not legally mandated, not one of the recognized mandatory-attorney 'attorney states') as well-corroborated industry-practitioner consensus rather than an independently pinned primary-source fact, consistent with this project's grounding-transparency standard for market-convention content (directly analogous to how the pa_re_broker bank flagged its own 'wet funding' classification as a market-convention hedge). Standard national real-estate content not tied to a specific Ohio statute -- appraisal theory (three approaches to value, depreciation, highest-and-best-use), federal RESPA/TILA/ECOA/TRID/Fair Housing Act history, general contract-law doctrine, real estate math formulas (commission splits, LTV, cap rate, NOI, proration, GRM), deed-type doctrine, and general business-entity concepts -- is flagged 'hedge: standard...' throughout, consistent with this project's grounding standard for generic/national content. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized Real Estate track rate, consistent with ny_re_broker.json, pa_re_broker.json, ca_re_broker.json, fl_re_broker.json, and tx_re_broker.json. Answer choices were drafted correct-as-choice_a throughout across all six parallel content-authoring passes, then deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_oh_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all questions in file order, not manual), yielding a final distribution of A: 77 (25.2%), B: 77 (25.2%), C: 76 (24.8%), D: 76 (24.8%) across all 306 questions (18 bucket files, capped at 17 questions each after an initial authoring pass produced 331 questions and the lowest-weight questions in over-target buckets were trimmed to bring the bank into this project's ~280-300-question target range while preserving each bucket's highest-yield content).
